newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods edge up amid NYMEX reversal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods edge up amid NYMEX reversal.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices rose after a flat morning session, tracking a reversal in NYMEX futures which saw crude oil break through a Post-Gulf War high of $26.10 a barrel.
West Coast spot trade saw most petroleum products rise a half cent late, as NYMEX gasoline negated a morning collapse with a 1.40 cent jump in prices.
Gasoline rose in line with crude, which rose 45 cents to settle $26.16 a barrel.

Refinery repairs kept prices from falling early, as NYMEX heating oil dipped 1.39 cents gallon amid forecasts of milder temperatures in the northeast region, the principal heating oil market in the U.S..
Late activity thinned out west in response to the sudden change in NYMEX's direction.
"It was a whiplash market for the NYMEX people and it kind of killed us," a broker said, referring to light afternoon trade.
January CARB gasoline was talked between 74.50 and 75.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, erasing an early 0.50 loss by rising 1.50 cents a gallon late.
Conventional also firmed with NYMEX, adding 0.50 cents to end 71.50/72.50 in late trade.
January CARB diesel was bid 73 cents a gallon in L.A., flat from Tuesday.
